The working file is the complete analysis and the reports are its reader copies — each should be read in full; this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

In brief: the recommendation is to **buy** a managed identity provider (WorkOS or Clerk, both ~free at your current scale per pricing pages I fetched directly) rather than build in-house, with three disciplines — abstract the auth boundary in your own code, lean on the vendor's standards-based OIDC/SAML/SCIM surface, and don't let sales claim "enterprise-ready" until SAML/SCIM is actually smoke-tested against a real IdP. The 5-Whys root-cause pass shows this isn't a one-off feature gap but a structural identity-model deficit, which reframes the real trade-off: buying converts your 12-18 month enterprise SSO/SCIM need into a metered billing event, while building risks paying the engineering cost twice — once now, under pressure, and again later, under even more pressure — while carrying six unverified security preconditions in the meantime. Confidence is MEDIUM overall (capped by a few unverified inputs — company-context facts and two secondary-sourced pricing/statistics citations); the full analysis names exactly what would raise or reverse this and includes a full pre-mortem with named mitigations for the vendor-dependency risk this recommendation accepts.
